name: Propylthiouracil Embryofetopathy

criteria.description: Documented maternal exposure to propylthiouracil during the first trimester of pregnancy
Presence of characteristic facial anomalies including choanal atresia or stenosis, and craniofacial dysmorphisms
Detection of congenital cardiovascular malformations such as ventricular septal defects or patent ductus arteriosus
Presence of skeletal abnormalities including limb defects or vertebral anomalies
Evidence of neonatal hypothyroidism or thyroid dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed maternal PTU exposure plus presence of at least two major congenital anomalies consistent with embryofetopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and based on history of PTU exposure combined with characteristic congenital malformations; genetic testing is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.notes: Bilateral or unilateral nasal passage obstruction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Craniofacial dysmorphism including micrognathia and low-set ears

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus)
searchTerms: abnormal heart structure present from birth

common.notes: Transient or permanent thyroid dysfunction in newborn

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to airway anomalies
common.notes: Secondary to choanal atresia or other airway malformations
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to airway issues

occasional.notes: Due to craniofacial anomalies or airway obstruction
Conductive or sensorineural hearing loss reported
Mild to moderate delays in some cases

searchTerms: problems with blood cells and clotting

laboratory: Neonatal thyroid function tests showing hypothyroidism
imaging: CT or MRI confirming choanal atresia
Skeletal X-rays showing limb or vertebral anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; diagnosis based on teratogenic exposure
other: Maternal history of propylthiouracil use during first trimester
Clinical examination revealing characteristic craniofacial and airway anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Exposure to methimazole instead of propylthiouracil
Presence of scalp defects (aplasia cutis) more common
Choanal atresia without history of PTU exposure
Associated with CHARGE syndrome or other genetic syndromes
Additional systemic anomalies distinct from PTU embryofetopathy

redFlags: History of maternal propylthiouracil use during first trimester
Neonatal respiratory distress due to choanal atresia
Presence of multiple congenital anomalies including heart defects and craniofacial dysmorphism
references: Cooper DS. Antithyroid drugs. N Engl J Med. 2005;352(9):905-917.
Momotani N, Noh JY, Ito K, et al. Propylthiouracil embryopathy: clinical features and teratogenicity. Thyroid. 2015;25(5):537-542.
